title: Book Three · Chapter 46: The Bus at Two
story:
The rest of spring passes. Hot mornings come, and school ends for the summer.

A week before the holiday, Leo's seventh reply arrives. His aunt has the tickets now. The bus will reach the main station at two on Saturday. The return bus leaves at ten on Wednesday morning.

They can have dinner at Ronan's home on Saturday. Mum and Dad agree to it. Leo's aunt will eat with her own family.

On Saturday, Ronan walks to the station with a full water bottle. He reaches the front doors before two.

People come out with bags and folded coats. A child drops a shoe. His father picks it up and carries both shoes in one hand.

Ronan watches the doors.

Then Leo comes through.

He looks taller. His hair is shorter too. His bag is over one shoulder. It is not across his chest.

For a moment, Ronan only stares.

Leo stops in front of him.

“Did the rice come?”

Ronan laughs. Then Leo pulls him into a quick hug. His bag hits Ronan's arm.

“Same bag,” Ronan says.

“Less paper inside.”

Leo's aunt comes through behind him. Leo introduces Ronan. She has a small case and a bag of fruit for the grandmother.

“We need to go there first,” she says. “She is expecting us.”

Ronan nods. They walk to the local bus stop together.

Leo's aunt pays for two tickets. Ronan uses a little of his own money for his seat. He has kept it for today. The aunt counts her change and puts it back in her purse.

On the bus, the boys sit beside each other. Leo points out a new shop. Ronan points to an empty place where an old stall stood.

“Gone?” Leo asks.

“The man moved nearer the market.”

“I need to look.”

At the stop, they get off with the aunt. The grandmother's door is only a short walk away.

Ronan waits outside while Leo goes in. He can hear a happy voice and a question about food.

Leo comes back to the doorway.

“She wants me to eat again.”

“You just arrived.”

“That seems to be the reason.”

The aunt looks over his shoulder. She wants Leo to sit with the family for a while. Ronan tells him he will be at home after four.

“Green door,” Leo says.

“Still green.”

They grin at each other.

Ronan says goodbye and takes the road toward West Lane. At a shop window, he sees his own face beside a row of jars.

He looks a little taller too.

At home, Mum asks if the bus arrived.

“Yes. He's here.”

The words make him smile again. He takes three cups from the shelf, then stops and adds a fourth for dinner.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

return bus＝返程公共汽车；ticket＝车票；expect＝等候、预期；grin＝咧嘴笑。

## 理解问题

1. 正式到暑假之前，哪封回信确认了车票和返程时间？
2. Leo下车后为什么没有立刻陪Ronan逛街？Ronan有没有要求他取消家人的安排？

## 读句子

**His bag is over one shoulder.**

拆开看：His bag / is / over one shoulder.

他的包／正搭着／搭在一边肩上。
